findings.title: Reschedule path still uses immediate SendGrid cancellation, which hits the 100-pending-cancel limit
findings.body: The PR exists because SendGrid allows at most 100 pending cancellations in `scheduled_sends`. Once that limit is reached, new cancels fail and the emails are still sent. Here `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` takes the immediate branch, which POSTs the cancel straight to SendGrid. The same immediate path is used in workflows.tsx for deleting a workflow and for deleted steps. Those flows can therefore still silently fail once the limit is reached, because the error is only logged. The reschedule flow does not need the immediate path, since the booking row still exists and the cron could cancel it later. Using the deferred `cancelled=true` flag there would avoid the limit.

findings.title: Fire-and-forget callers may drop the `cancelled` flag update
findings.body: Marking the reminder `cancelled: true` is the only thing that now stops the email from being sent. The callers in bookings.tsx, handleCancelBooking.ts and workflows.tsx do not `await` this call. The old code awaited the DB deletes via `Promise.all`. In serverless runtimes, un-awaited work can be frozen or dropped once the response is returned, so the DB write may never happen. The cron would then never cancel that reminder and the email would still go out. These calls should be awaited, for example with `Promise.all`.

findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts all remaining cancellations and deletions
findings.body: The whole cancel loop is inside a single try/catch. If any `client.request` call throws, for example from a rate limit or a bad batch id, the loop exits. Remaining reminders are not cancelled, and none of the queued `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises run, because they are lazy and only awaited after the loop. A single bad reminder with an invalid referenceId can therefore block every later cancellation on every cron run. Each reminder should be handled in its own try/catch. Reminders that SendGrid reports as already gone should be deleted rather than retried forever.

findings.title: Cancellation window can be missed for late cancellations and is not limited to EMAIL
findings.body: The cron runs every 15 minutes and only cancels reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour. A booking cancelled shortly before the send time, between two cron runs, may not be picked up in time. In that case the reminder is deleted by the earlier `deleteMany` only after its scheduled time has passed, and the email has already been sent. The query also does not filter on `method: EMAIL`, unlike the other queries in this file.

findings.title: Unused value import and unrelated reformatting of commented code
findings.body: `Prisma` is now imported as a runtime value, but nothing in the file uses it after the removal of the `PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>` code. The list also lacks a trailing comma. The diff additionally strips the indentation of the large commented-out `testAction` block, which adds noise unrelated to the fix.

findings.title: Unrelated UI refactor bundled into the bug-fix PR
findings.body: The phone-number block's wrapper condition changes from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded`, and the markup is reindented. This has nothing to do with cancelling workflow reminders. It changes rendering behaviour for SMS_ATTENDEE, where an empty gray box is no longer shown. It should be a separate change, or at least be mentioned in the PR description.
